blocking_failures: anti_cheating_measures: The HMAC key in /app/etc/audit.key is baked into the image and available to the agent at runtime. The tests also read this key file to compute expected HMACs. Since the agent can read the same key file, it could potentially hardcode results. More critically, the test inputs (txid values, payloads) are fixed and match the seeded database rows exactly - an agent that memorized the test file could craft a trivially passing solution. However the main concern is that the solution fix targets are discoverable from the source code, so this is a borderline case. The bigger issue is allow_internet=true in task.toml, which could allow the agent to look up hints.
advice: verify_time_inputs: All test inputs (txid values, payloads, expected charge_txid mappings) exactly match the rows seeded in init_db.py and are visible to the agent in the environment. Tests do not generate fresh inputs or use values outside the seeded dataset. An agent could potentially craft a solution that only handles the specific test cases without implementing the general logic correctly.
